questions.question: For a triangle ABC, D and E are two points on AB and AC such that AD = (1)/(6) AB, AE = (1)/(6) AC. If BC = 22 cm, then DE is ___________. (Consider up to two decimals)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AD = (1)/(6) AB

AE = (1)/(6) AC

BC = 22 cm

**Concept Used:**

If two sides in one triangle are proportional to two sides in another triangle and the included angle in both are congruent, then the two triangles are similar.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/32b92596ba02c6afe83a2f2d44974a00ad2bb7204aa2470be50c7c5d70bb06ea.png] 

In Δ ABC and Δ ADE

∠ BAC = ∠ DAC (Same angle)

(AD)/(AB) = (1)/(6) ; (AE)/(AC) = (1)/(6)

By using the Side-Angle-Side similarity theorem we can say that Δ ABC and Δ ADE are similar.

Hence, (AD)/(AB) = (AE)/(AC) = (DE)/(BC) = (1)/(6)

⇒ (DE)/(22) = (1)/(6)

⇒ DE = 22/6 = 3.667cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.67cm.**

questions.question: The least common multiple of 210, 336 and 504 is :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the HCF of 210, 336, and 504 which is 42.

Divide the numbers by 42 to get the ratios: 5, 8, and 12.

The LCM of the remaining ratios (5, 8, 12) is 120.

Total LCM = HCF × LCM of ratios = 42 × 120 = 5040.

**∴ The correct answer is 5040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given values: 210, 336, 504

Method: Prime Factorization Method

⇒ 210 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ 336 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 = 2⁴ × 3 × 7

⇒ 504 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 7 = 2³ × 3² × 7

⇒ LCM = Highest power of each prime factor present in the numbers

⇒ LCM = 2⁴ × 3² × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 16 × 9 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 144 × 35

⇒ LCM = 5040

**∴ The correct answer is 5040.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM × HCF Relation

For any two numbers a and b, Product of numbers (a × b) = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

LCM of Fractions

LCM of a group of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators.

HCF of Numbers

HCF is the greatest number that divides each of the given numbers without leaving a remainder.</p

questions.question: A hostel mess requires 217 eggs for a week. How many eggs will it require in total for the months of July, August and September?
questions.solution:
Concept Used: 

7 days a week.

Formula:

Sum of the observations = Average × No. of observations

Divide total no of eggs in 7 days for one week. And then count the months days and multiply with per days eggs.

Calculation:

Each day egg consumption = 217/7 = 31 

Months of days in July, August, and September = 31 + 31+ 30 = 92 days

Total egg consumption in three months = 92 × 31 = 2852

∴ 2852 eggs will be required for the months of July, August, and September.

questions.question: The cost of painting the total surface area of a 30 m high solid right circular cylinder at the rate of Rs. 25 per m² is Rs. 18,425. What is the volume (in m³) of this cylinder [use π = (22)/(7)]?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Total Surface Area (TSA)** = **Total Cost** ÷ **Rate** = 18425 ÷ 25 = 737 m².

TSA = 2πr(h + r) ⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r(30 + r) = 737.

r(30 + r) = 117.25 ⇒ r = 3.5 m (by solving the quadratic equation or trial).

**Volume** = πr²h = (22/7) × (3.5)² × 30 = 1155 m³.

**∴ The correct answer is 1155 m³.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Height (h)** = 30 m, **Rate** = ₹ 25/m², **Total Cost** = ₹ 18,425, π = 22/7.

**Formula Used:** **Total Surface Area** of cylinder = 2πr(h + r); **Volume** = πr²h.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd2176bbb560a24c95698d784ff10246fd813bcb24702d2cd6e8a924fd4893a0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Surface Area (TSA)** = 18425 ÷ 25 = 737 m²

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r × (30 + r) = 737

⇒ (44/7) × (30r + r²) = 737

⇒ 30r + r² = (737 × 7) ÷ 44 = 67 × 7 ÷ 4 = 117.25

⇒ r² + 30r − 117.25 = 0

⇒ 4r² + 120r − 469 = 0

⇒ Applying quadratic formula: r = [−120 + √(120² − 4 × 4 × (−469))] ÷ (2 × 4)

⇒ r = [−120 + √(14400 + 7504)] ÷ 8 = [−120 + √21904] ÷ 8

⇒ r = (−120 + 148) ÷ 8 = 28 ÷ 8 = 3.5 m

⇒ **Volume** = (22/7) × (3.5)² × 30

⇒ **Volume** = (22/7) × 12.25 × 30 = 22 × 1.75 × 30 = 1155 m³

**∴ The correct answer is 1155 m³.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Mensuration Formulas

For a cylinder with **radius (r)** and **height (h)**, the Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2πrh and the base area is πr².

Total Surface Area (TSA)

TSA includes the curved part and both flat circular ends: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume Property

The volume represents the **capacity** of the cylinder, calculated as V = Area of base × height = πr²h.

questions.question: John can do a piece of work alone in 20 days, while Ravi can do the same piece of work alone in 28 days. In how many days can the duo complete the same work if they work together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by John to complete a piece of work = 20 days

Time taken by Ravi to complete a piece of work = 28 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total work/Time taken to complete the work.

**Calculation:**

Total work = LCM of (20 and 28) = 140

Efficiency of John = Total work/Time taken to complete a piece of work = 140/20 = 7

Efficiency of Ravi = Total work/Time taken to complete a piece of work = 140/28 = 5

Total time taken by them working together to complete the work = Total work/total efficiency

⇒ (140)/(7 + 5) = 35/3 = 11(2)/(3)

**∴ The correct answer is 11(2)/(3) days.**

questions.question: The volume of a right circular cone having a base diameter of 14 cm is 196 π cm³.Find the perpendicular height of this cone
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Radius (r)** = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

**Volume (V)** = (1/3) × π × r² × h

196π = (1/3) × π × 49 × h ⇒ 196 = (49/3) × h

h = (196 × 3) ÷ 49 = 4 × 3 = 12 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Base Diameter** of the cone (d) = 14 cm

⇒ **Volume** of the cone (V) = 196π cm³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae9ea32d767c15e253e72a487c288db8dd19078b28dc277573776967be30f200.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a **right circular cone** = (1/3) × π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Radius (r)** = Diameter ÷ 2 = 14 ÷ 2 = 7 cm

⇒ 196π = (1/3) × π × (7)² × h

⇒ 196π = (1/3) × π × 49 × h

⇒ 196 = (49/3) × h

⇒ h = (196 × 3) ÷ 49

⇒ h = 4 × 3

⇒ h = 12 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 12 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Slant Height of Cone

The slant height (l) is the distance from the apex to any point on the base circle: l = √(r² + h²).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved surface of a right circular cone is given by the formula: CSA = πrl.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Relation with Cylinder

The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3rd of the volume of a cylinder having the same base radius and height.</p

questions.question: Find the greatest possible length (in meters) that can be used to exactly measure the lengths 6 m, 5 m 25 cm, and 12 m 50 cm.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the **greatest possible length**, calculate the **HCF** of the given values.

Convert all units to cm: 600 cm, 525 cm, and 1250 cm.

HCF(600, 525, 1250) → Difference method: 600 − 525 = 75. Factors of 75 are 1, 3, 5, 15, 25, 75.

Check 25: 600/25 = 24, 525/25 = 21, 1250/25 = 50. All divisible.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Lengths are 6 m, 5 m 25 cm, and 12 m 50 cm.

**Formula Used:** Required length = **HCF** (Length₁, Length₂, Length₃)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46fb65dfaa0e912944dda70833b89f4a2c5b8f1d61918e00d789fd742b7ebc9d.png] 

⇒ Conversion: 6 m = 600 cm

⇒ Conversion: 5 m 25 cm = (5 × 100) + 25 = 525 cm

⇒ Conversion: 12 m 50 cm = (12 × 100) + 50 = 1250 cm

⇒ Prime Factorization:

⇒ 600 = 2³ × 3 × 5²

⇒ 525 = 3 × 5² × 7

⇒ 1250 = 2 × 5⁴

⇒ HCF = 5² = 25 cm

⇒ Convert back to meters: 25 ÷ 100 = 0.25 m

**∴ The correct answer is 0.25 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the **greatest number** that divides each of the two or more numbers without leaving a remainder.

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The **smallest non-zero common number** which is a multiple of all the given numbers.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of (a/b, c/d) = HCF(a, c) ÷ LCM(b, d).

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all measurements are in the **same unit** before calculating HCF or LCM. 1 meter = 100 centimeters.</p

questions.question: Reema runs (5)/(4) times as fast as Rekha. In view of this Reema allows Rekha a lead of 50 metres to Rekha in a friendly race competition. What is the distance from the starting point where both Reema and Rekha meet?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Reema = (5/4) × Speed of Rekha

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of Rekha = A m/s

Speed of Reema = (5/4) × A

Relative Speed between Reema and Rekha = Difference between their Speed.

⇒ (5A)/(4) - A = A/4

Time taken by Reema to cover the gap of 50m = 50/Relative Speed

⇒ (50)/(frac{A){4}} = 200/A m/s

Total distance covered by Reema (while covering the gap) = Speed of Reema × Time taken by Reema to cover the gap

⇒ (5A)/(4) times (200)/(A) = 250m

**∴ The correct answer is 250m.**

questions.question: Train ‘A’ requires 15 seconds to cross train ‘B’ of length 300 m moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 36 km/h. Further, train ‘A’ requires 30 seconds to cross a 500 m long stationary train ‘C’. Find the length (in m) of train ‘A’.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train B = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

For Train A to cross Train B, relative speed = Speed to cross stationary C + Speed of B.

⇒ (LA + 300) ÷ 15 = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 + 10

⇒ 2LA + 600 = LA + 500 + 300

⇒ LA = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train B = 300 m

Speed of train B = 36 km/h = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

Length of stationary train C = 500 m

Time to cross B = 15 s, Time to cross C = 30 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769276248a78aa7449ab538025ee5c0e35cc38fac6df147a92bbfaa750d86c87.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of train A be LA and its speed be VA.

⇒ Time taken to cross train B = (LA + 300) ÷ (VA + 10) = 15

⇒ VA + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15 --- (1)

⇒ Time taken to cross stationary train C = (LA + 500) ÷ VA = 30

⇒ VA = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 --- (2)

⇒ Substituting equation (2) into equation (1):

⇒ [(LA + 500) ÷ 30] + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15

⇒ Multiplying by 30 on both sides:

⇒ LA + 500 + 300 = 2 × (LA + 300)

⇒ LA + 800 = 2LA + 600

⇒ LA = 800 − 600 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂). For the same direction, it is the difference (V₁ − V₂).

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses an object with length (like a platform or another train), the total distance covered equals the sum of lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
